paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “With the increasing application of AI technology, there is a growing concern that it may negatively impact human creativity.” You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有 30 分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“随着人工智能技术的应用不断增加，人们越来越担心它可能会对人类创造力产生负面影响。”您可以发表评论、引用示例或利用您的个人经历来完善您的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: You should copy the sentence given in quotes at the beginning of your essay.
paragraphs.translationZh: 您应该复制论文开头引号中给出的句子。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: No beast on Earth is tougher than the tiny tardigrade (缓步类动物). It can 26 being frozen at −272º Celsius, being exposed to the vacuum of outer space and even being 27 with 500 times the dose of X-rays that would kill a human. In other words, the creature can endure conditions that don’t even exist on Earth. And researchers are looking to the microscopic animals to learn how to prepare humans and crops to handle the 28 of space travel.
paragraphs.translationZh: 地球上没有任何野兽比微小的缓步类动物更坚强。它可以在-272摄氏度的冰冻、暴露在外太空的真空中，甚至在足以杀死人类的500倍X射线照射下生存。换句话说，这种生物可以忍受地球上不存在的条件。研究人员正在研究微观动物，以了解如何让人类和农作物做好准备以应对太空旅行的严酷考验。

paragraphs.sourceText: The tardigrade’s indestructibility stems from its 29 to its environment — which may seem surprising, since it lives in 30 comfortable places, like the cool, wet patches of moss (青苔) that dot a garden wall.
paragraphs.translationZh: 缓步动物的坚不可摧源于它对环境的适应——这似乎令人惊讶，因为它生活在看似舒适的地方，比如点缀在花园墙上的凉爽潮湿的青苔。

paragraphs.sourceText: But it turns out that a tardigrade’s damp, mossy home can dry out many times each year. Drying is pretty 31 for most living things. It does damage to cells in some of the same ways that freezing, vacuum and radiation do. Tardigrades, however, have 32 special strategies for dealing with these kinds of damage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但事实证明，缓步动物潮湿、长满青苔的家园每年都会多次变干。干燥对于大多数生物来说都是灾难性的。它对细胞的损害与冷冻、真空和辐射的某些方式相同。然而，缓步动物已经进化出特殊的策略来应对此类伤害。

paragraphs.sourceText: As a tardigrade dries out, its cells produce several strange proteins that are unlike anything found in other animals. In water, the proteins are shapeless. But as water disappears, the proteins self-assemble into long fibers that fill the cell’s 33 . The fibers support the cell’s membranes (细胞膜) and proteins, preventing them from breaking or 34 .
paragraphs.translationZh: 当缓步动物变干时，它的细胞会产生几种奇怪的蛋白质，这些蛋白质与其他动物中发现的任何蛋白质都不同。在水中，蛋白质是无形状的。但随着水消失，蛋白质会自组装成长纤维，填充细胞内部。纤维支撑细胞膜（细胞膜）和蛋白质，防止它们破裂或展开。

paragraphs.sourceText: Emulating tardigrades could one day help humans colonize outer space. Food crops could be engineered to produce tardigrade proteins, allowing these organisms to grow more efficiently on spacecraft where levels of radiation are elevated compared with on Earth.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有一天，模仿缓步动物可能会帮助人类殖民外太空。粮食作物可以被改造为产生缓步动物蛋白质，使这些生物体能够在辐射水平高于地球的航天器上更有效地生长。

paragraphs.sourceText: So if humans ever succeed in reaching the stars, they may accomplish this 35 , in part, by standing on the shoulders of the tiny eight-legged endurance specialists in your backyard.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，如果人类成功到达星星，他们可能会通过站在后院微小的八足耐力专家的肩膀上来完成这一壮举。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Yes, Eating Meat Affects the Environment, but Cows Are Not Killing the Climate
paragraphs.translationZh: 是的，吃肉会影响环境，但奶牛并没有破坏气候

paragraphs.sourceText: A) As the scale and impacts of climate change become increasingly alarming, meat is a popular target for action. Advocates for the protection of the natural environment from destruction or pollution urge the public to eat less meat. Some activists have even called for taxing meat to reduce consumption of it.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 随着气候变化的规模和影响变得越来越令人担忧，肉类成为受欢迎的行动目标。保护自然环境免受破坏或污染的倡导者敦促公众少吃肉。一些活动人士甚至呼吁对肉类征税以减少肉类消费。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) A key claim underlying these arguments holds that globally, meat production generates more greenhouse gases than the entire transportation sector. However, this claim is demonstrably wrong, as I will show. And its persistence has led to false assumptions about the linkage between meat and climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）这些论点背后的一个关键主张是，在全球范围内，肉类生产产生的温室气体比整个运输部门产生的温室气体还要多。然而，正如我将证明的那样，这种说法显然是错误的。它的持续存在导致人们对肉类与气候变化之间的联系产生了错误的假设。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) My recent research focuses on ways in which animal agriculture affects air quality and climate change. In my view, there are many reasons for either choosing animal protein or opting for a vegetarian selection. However, abandoning meat and meat products is not the environmental panacea (万灵药) many would have us believe. And if taken to an extreme, it also could have harmful nutritional consequences.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 我最近的研究重点是畜牧业影响空气质量和气候变化的方式。在我看来，选择动物蛋白或选择素食有很多原因。然而，放弃肉类和肉制品并不是许多人想让我们相信的万灵药。如果走向极端，它还可能产生有害的营养后果。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) A healthy portion of meat’s negative reputation centers on the assertion that livestock is the largest source of greenhouse gases worldwide. For example, an analysis published in 2009 by the World Watch Institute based in Washington, D.C. asserted that 51 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions come from rearing and processing livestock. According to the US Environmental Protection Agency, the largest sources of US greenhouse gas emissions in 2016 were electricity production (28 percent of total emissions), transportation (28 percent) and industry (22 percent). All of agriculture accounted for a total of 9 percent, but all of animal agriculture contributes less than half of this amount, representing 3.9 percent of the total greenhouse emission in the US. That is very different from claiming that livestock represents as much as or more than transportation.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 肉类负面声誉的一个健康部分集中在这样的断言上：牲畜是全球最大的温室气体来源。例如，总部位于华盛顿特区的世界观察研究所 2009 年发表的一份分析报告称，全球温室气体排放量的 51% 来自牲畜饲养和加工。根据美国环境保护署的数据，2016年美国温室气体排放的最大来源是电力生产（占总排放量的28%）、交通运输（28%）和工业（22%）。所有农业总共占9%，但所有畜牧业的贡献不到这一数字的一半，占美国温室气体排放总量的3.9%。这与声称牲畜与运输同等重要或更多的说法截然不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) Why is there such a misconception? In 2006 the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) published a study titled “Livestock’s Long Shadow,” which received widespread international attention. It stated that livestock produced a staggering 18 percent of the world’s greenhouse gas emissions. The agency drew a startling conclusion that livestock was doing more to harm the climate than all modes of transportation combined. This latter claim was wrong, and has since been corrected by Henning Stenfeld, the report’s senior author.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 为什么会有这样的误解？ 2006年，联合国粮食及农业组织（FAO）发表了题为《牲畜的长影》的研究报告，受到国际社会广泛关注。报告指出，畜牧业产生的温室气体排放量占全球温室气体排放量的 18%，这一比例令人震惊。该机构得出了一个令人震惊的结论：牲畜对气候的危害比所有运输方式的总和还多。后一种说法是错误的，该报告的资深作者亨宁·斯坦菲尔德已纠正了这一说法。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The problem was that analysts from the FAO used a comprehensive life-cycle assessment to study the climate impact of livestock, but a different method when they analyzed transportation. For livestock, they considered every factor associated with producing meat. This included emissions from fertilizer production, converting land from forests to pastures, growing feed, and direct emissions from animals (manure as well as expelling of gas from the stomach) from birth to death.
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 问题在于，粮农组织的分析人员使用了全面的生命周期评估来研究牲畜对气候的影响，但在分析运输时却采用了不同的方法。对于牲畜，他们考虑了与生产肉类相关的每一个因素。这包括化肥生产、将土地从森林转变为牧场、种植饲料的排放，以及动物从出生到死亡的直接排放（粪便以及胃中排出的气体）。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) However, when they looked at transportation’s carbon footprint, they ignored impacts on the climate from manufacturing vehicle materials and parts, assembling vehicles and maintaining roads, bridges and airports. Instead, they only considered the exhaust smoke emitted by finished cars, trucks, trains and planes. As a result, the FAO’s comparison of greenhouse gas emissions from livestock to those from transportation was greatly distorted.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 然而，当他们考虑交通运输的碳足迹时，他们忽略了制造车辆材料和零部件、组装车辆以及维护道路、桥梁和机场对气候的影响。相反，他们只考虑成品汽车、卡车、火车和飞机排放的废气。结果，粮农组织对牲畜和交通运输温室气体排放的比较严重扭曲。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) I pointed out this flaw during a speech to fellow scientists in San Francisco on March 22, 2010, which led to a flood of media coverage. To its credit, the FAO immediately owned up to its error. Unfortunately, the agency’s initial claim that livestock was responsible for the lion’s share of world greenhouse gas emissions had already received wide coverage. To this day, we struggle to “unring” the bell. In its most recent assessment report, the FAO estimated that livestock produces 14.5 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions from human activities. There is no comparable full life-cycle assessment for transportation. However, as Stenfeld has pointed out, direct emissions from transportation versus livestock can be compared and amount to 14 versus 5 percent, respectively.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 我在 2010 年 3 月 22 日在旧金山向科学家同行发表演讲时指出了这个缺陷，引起了媒体的大量报道。值得赞扬的是，粮农组织立即承认了自己的错误。不幸的是，该机构最初声称畜牧业造成了世界温室气体排放的大部分，这一说法已经得到了广泛的报道。直到今天，我们仍在努力“敲响”警钟。粮农组织在其最新评估报告中估计，畜牧业产生的温室气体排放量占人类活动全球温室气体排放量的 14.5%。目前尚无可比的运输全生命周期评估。然而，正如 Stenfeld 指出的那样，交通运输和牲畜产生的直接排放量可以进行比较，分别达到 14% 和 5%。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Many people continue to think that avoiding meat as infrequently as once a week will make a significant difference to the climate. But according to one recent study, even if Americans eliminated all animal protein from their diets, they would reduce US greenhouse gas emissions by only 2.6 percent. According to our research at the University of California, Davis, if the practice of Meatless Monday were to be adopted by all Americans, we’d see a reduction of only 0.5 percent.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 许多人仍然认为，每周一次不吃肉会对气候产生重大影响。但根据最近的一项研究，即使美国人从饮食中消除所有动物蛋白，他们也只能将美国温室气体排放量减少 2.6%。根据我们在加州大学戴维斯分校的研究，如果所有美国人都采用周一无肉的做法，我们只会看到减少 0.5%。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Moreover, technological, genetic and management changes that have taken place in US agriculture over the past 70 years have made livestock production more efficient and less greenhouse gas-intensive. According to the FAO’s statistical database, total direct greenhouse gas emissions from US livestock have declined by 11.3 percent since 1961, while production of livestock meat has more than doubled.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 此外，过去 70 年美国农业在技术、遗传和管理方面发生的变化使畜牧业生产更加高效，温室气体排放也更少。根据联合国粮农组织的统计数据库，自1961年以来，美国牲畜直接温室气体排放总量下降了11.3%，而牲畜肉类产量却增加了一倍多。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) Demand for meat is rising in developing and emerging economies, especially in the Middle East, North Africa and Southeast Asia. For example, raising livestock such as goats in Kenya is an important source of food and income for many small-scale farmers and herders. But meat consumption per person in these regions still lags that of developed countries. In 2015, average annual meat consumption per person in developed countries was 92 kilograms, compared to 24 kilograms in the Middle East and North Africa and 18 kilograms in Southeast Asia. Still, given projected population growth in the developing world, there will certainly be an opportunity for countries such as the United States to bring their sustainable livestock rearing practices to the table.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 发展中经济体和新兴经济体对肉类的需求正在上升，特别是在中东、北非和东南亚。例如，在肯尼亚饲养山羊等牲畜是许多小规模农牧民的重要食物和收入来源。但这些地区的人均肉类消费量仍落后于发达国家。 2015年，发达国家人均肉类年消费量为92公斤，而中东和北非为24公斤，东南亚为18公斤。尽管如此，考虑到发展中国家预计的人口增长，美国等国家肯定有机会将其可持续牲畜饲养实践摆上桌面。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) Removing animals from US agriculture would lower national greenhouse gas emissions to a small degree, but it would also make it harder to meet people’s nutritional requirements. Many critics of animal agriculture are quick to point out that if farmers raised only plants, they could produce more pounds of food and more calories per person. But humans also need many essential micro- and macro-nutrients for good health. It’s hard to make a compelling argument that the United States has a calorie deficit, given its high national rates of adult and child obesity. Moreover, not all plant parts are edible or desirable. Raising livestock is a way to add nutritional and economic value to plant agriculture.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 将动物从美国农业中剔除会在一定程度上降低国家温室气体排放，但也会使满足人们的营养需求变得更加困难。许多畜牧业批评者很快指出，如果农民只种植植物，他们每人可以生产更多磅的食物和更多的卡路里。但人类还需要许多必需的微量和大量营养素来保持健康。鉴于美国全国成人和儿童肥胖率很高，很难提出令人信服的论据来证明美国存在卡路里短缺。此外，并非所有植物部分都是可食用或理想的。饲养牲畜是增加植物农业营养和经济价值的一种方式。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) As one example, the energy in plants that livestock consume is most often contained in cellulose (纤维素), which is indigestible for humans and many other mammals. But cows, sheep and other ruminant (反刍的) animals can break cellulose down and release the solar energy contained in this vast resource. According to the FAO, as much as 70 percent of all agricultural land globally is range land that can only be utilized as grazing land for ruminant livestock.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 举一个例子，牲畜消耗的植物中的能量通常包含在纤维素（纤维素）中，而人类和许多其他哺乳动物无法消化纤维素。但牛、羊和其他反刍动物可以分解纤维素并释放这一巨大资源中所含的太阳能。据联合国粮农组织称，全球 70% 的农业用地都是牧场，只能用作反刍牲畜的牧场。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The world population is currently projected to reach 9.8 billion by 2050. Feeding this many people will raise immense challenges. Meat is more calorie-dense per serving than vegetarian options, and ruminant animals largely thrive on feed that is not suitable for humans. Raising livestock also offers much-needed income for small-scale farmers in developing nations. Worldwide, livestock provides a livelihood for 1 billion people.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 目前，世界人口预计到 2050 年将达到 98 亿。养活这么多人将带来巨大的挑战。每份肉类的热量密度比素食更高，而反刍动物主要依靠不适合人类的饲料来茁壮成长。饲养牲畜还为发展中国家的小农提供了急需的收入。在世界范围内，畜牧业为 10 亿人提供了生计。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Climate change demands urgent attention, and the livestock industry has a large overall environmental footprint that affects air, water and land. These, combined with a rapidly rising world population, give us plenty of compelling reasons to continue to work for greater efficiencies in animal agriculture. I believe the place to start is with science-based facts.
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 气候变化需要迫切关注，畜牧业对空气、水和土地的整体环境足迹很大。这些，再加上世界人口的迅速增长，给了我们充足的理由继续努力提高畜牧业的效率。我相信首先要从基于科学的事实开始。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. The FAO concluded that farm animals were producing more greenhouse gases than all modes of transportation combined.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 粮农组织的结论是，农场动物产生的温室气体比所有运输方式的总和还要多。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Consumption of meat per person in developing countries is much less than that in countries like the US.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 发展中国家的人均肉类消费量远低于美国等国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. The FAO was worthy of praise in that it admitted its mistake once it was pointed out.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 值得称赞的是，粮农组织在被指出错误后就承认了。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Environmentalists try hard to make people consume less meat to combat climate change.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 环保主义者努力让人们少吃肉来应对气候变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Recent research has shown that even if Americans quit eating meat altogether, the resulting reduction of greenhouse gases in the US would be slight.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 最近的研究表明，即使美国人完全戒掉肉食，美国温室气体的减少也将是轻微的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. More than half of the world’s farmland is suitable only for animals like cows to graze on.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 世界上一半以上的农田只适合牛等动物吃草。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. The allegation that farm animals produce the world’s largest portion of greenhouse gases is responsible for meat’s bad reputation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 有人指控农场动物产生了世界上最大的温室气体，这是造成肉类声誉不佳的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. Raising farm animals makes it easier to meet people’s nutritional needs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 饲养农场动物更容易满足人们的营养需求。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. The author doesn’t believe giving up meat and meat products will be a cure-all for the environmental problem.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 作者并不认为放弃肉类和肉制品能够解决环境问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. Changes in America’s farming technology and management in the past decades have increased efficiency and reduced greenhouse gas emissions in meat production.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 过去几十年美国农业技术和管理的变化提高了肉类生产的效率并减少了温室气体排放。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Why are we so worried about our careers? Partly it’s to do with money, but there’s a psychological aspect to our fears as well.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为什么我们如此担心我们的职业生涯？部分原因与金钱有关，但我们的恐惧也有心理方面的原因。

paragraphs.sourceText: We worry because we suspect — not wrongly — that the world is full of a frightening sort of person ready to judge us ruthlessly and swiftly: a person we can call a snob.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们担心是因为我们怀疑——这并没有错——世界上充满了一种可怕的人，他们准备无情而迅速地评判我们：我们可以称之为势利小人。

paragraphs.sourceText: A snob is anyone who takes a relatively small part of us and uses it to come to a rigid conclusion about how much of their attention we deserve. In the past, that might be your ancestry and royal connections. Nowadays, the snob cares about one thing only: what you do for a living.
paragraphs.translationZh: 势利小人是指那些只占我们相对较小部分的人，并用它来得出我们应该得到多少他们的关注的严格结论。在过去，这可能是你的血统和皇室​​关系。如今，势利小人只关心一件事：你以什么为生。

paragraphs.sourceText: This explains why the first question we will be asked in any new social context is “What do you do?” and according to how we answer, snobs will either welcome us with broad smiles, or leave us in the cold.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这解释了为什么我们在任何新的社会环境中都会被问到的第一个问题是“你做什么？”根据我们的回答，势利小人要么以灿烂的笑容欢迎我们，要么对我们冷落。

paragraphs.sourceText: And that is why we are fired up by such a desperate urge to achieve and impress.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么我们如此迫切地渴望取得成就并给人留下深刻印象。

paragraphs.sourceText: Sometimes our behaviour is mistaken for greed and vanity, but it is more than this. A lot of our interest in fancy cars, jobs and houses has nothing to do with materialism. It has to do with a hunger for the respect and esteem that is only available in our societies through the acquisition of material goods. It isn’t the goods themselves we seek, it is the love we stand to gain through our possession of them. The next time we see someone driving a Ferrari, we shouldn’t condemn them for their greed, we should pity them for the intensity of their need for love from the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有时我们的行为会被误认为是贪婪和虚荣，但事实还不止于此。我们对豪华汽车、工作和房屋的很多兴趣与物质主义无关。它与对尊重和尊重的渴望有关，而这种渴望在我们的社会中只能通过获得物质财富才能获得。我们追求的不是物品本身，而是我们通过拥有它们而获得的爱。下次当我们看到有人驾驶法拉利时，我们不应该谴责他们的贪婪，我们应该怜悯他们对世界爱的强烈需求。

paragraphs.sourceText: At the root of snobbery is a lack of imagination and confidence about how to decide who in the world is valuable. The snobs are brutally misguided and slavish in their beliefs about how the superior individuals can be identified. For snobs, it is the already acclaimed and already successful who are the only ones worthy of respect. There is no room in their timid regimented minds to imagine that someone might be clever, kind or good — and yet somehow have been overlooked entirely by society, their qualities lying hidden beneath an unfamiliar veil and having as yet discovered no obvious outlet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 势利的根源在于对于如何决定世界上谁是有价值的缺乏想象力和信心。势利小人在如何识别优秀个体的信念上被严重误导和奴役。对于势利小人来说，只有那些已经广受赞誉、已经成功的人才是唯一值得尊重的人。在他们胆怯、受管制的头脑中，没有空间去想象某人可能是聪明、善良或善良的，但不知何故却被社会完全忽视了，他们的品质隐藏在陌生的面纱下，至今还没有发现明显的出路。

paragraphs.sourceText: The true answer to snobbery is not to say that there is no such thing as a better or worse person, but to insist that better or worse exist in constantly unexpected places and carry none of the outward signs of distinction. And because we are such poor judges of the worth of others, our ultimate duty remains to be kind, good, curious and imaginative about pretty much everyone who ever crosses our path.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对势利的真正回答并不是说没有好人或坏人之分，而是坚持认为好人或坏人总是存在于意想不到的地方，并且没有任何外在的区别标志。因为我们对其他人的价值判断能力很差，所以我们的最终责任仍然是对几乎所有遇到我们的人表现出友善、善良、好奇和富有想象力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Women have historically been paid less. But in the US in the 1980s, they began to catch up — fast. During that decade, the gender pay gap closed by about one percentage point a year. Had that trend continued, the gender wage gap would have been closed by 2017.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从历史上看，女性的工资一直较低。但在 20 世纪 80 年代的美国，他们开始快速迎头赶上。在那十年里，性别工资差距每年缩小约一个百分点。如果这种趋势持续下去，性别工资差距到 2017 年就会缩小。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the trend didn’t continue, and the gap remains yawning.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但这种趋势并没有持续下去，而且差距仍然在扩大。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to a new study from academics at Harvard, the stagnation can be put down, perhaps counterintuitively, to the introduction of state and federal family leave policies.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据哈佛大学学者的一项新研究，这种停滞可以归因于州和联邦家庭休假政策的出台，这或许与直觉相反。

paragraphs.sourceText: The academics argue that during the 1990s, as governments began to introduce leave policies, it was mainly women who took advantage of them. Though the leave policies might have helped those women to stay in the workplace — instead of dropping out to have families — those who returned saw their wages had increased at lower rates than the men.
paragraphs.translationZh: 学者们认为，在 20 世纪 90 年代，当政府开始引入休假政策时，主要是女性利用了这些政策。尽管休假政策可能有助于这些女性留在工作场所，而不是为了组建家庭而辍学，但那些返回的女性发现她们的工资增幅低于男性。

paragraphs.sourceText: After family leave was introduced in the US, in fact, the rate of gender wage convergence fell to just 0.03 percentage points per year, and has remained there ever since.
paragraphs.translationZh: 事实上，在美国引入家事假后，性别工资趋同率每年下降至仅 0.03 个百分点，并且此后一直保持这一水平。

paragraphs.sourceText: Those monitoring the process towards salary equity at work have long watched as progress slowed in many countries around the world. In fact, that progress began to reverse during the pandemic (大流行病).
paragraphs.translationZh: 那些监控工作中薪资公平进程的人们长期以来一直关注着世界上许多国家的进展放缓。事实上，这种进展在大流行病期间开始逆转。

paragraphs.sourceText: The gender pay gap is one of the most outstanding examples of that lack of parity (平等), and still exists just about everywhere. The motherhood penalty has become a shorthand for describing why: In many places, especially rich countries, women earn the same as men until they reach their childbearing years. Women who have children begin to see their salaries slip behind their male counterparts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 性别工资差距是缺乏平等的最突出的例子之一，而且几乎在任何地方仍然存在。母亲的惩罚已成为描述其原因的简写：在许多地方，尤其是富裕国家，女性在达到育龄之前的收入与男性相同。有孩子的女性开始发现她们的工资落后于男性。

paragraphs.sourceText: Part of this is because women take on more of the unpaid labor at home, which can eat into time available for work and energy for career advancement. But it’s also because mothers are passed over for raises and promotion, and because time out of the workplace sets women back, even if that time is taken voluntarily, and supported by company or government policy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 部分原因是女性在家里承担了更多的无偿劳动，这会消耗可用于工作的时间和职业发展的精力。但这也是因为母亲在加薪和晋升方面被忽视，而且因为离开工作场所的时间会让女性退缩，即使这些时间是自愿占用的，并得到公司或政府政策的支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: What would have happened if leave policies hadn’t been introduced? The study doesn’t go into that question, other than to say that if the 1980s trend continued, we would have been at parity by now.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果没有出台休假政策，会发生什么？这项研究没有探讨这个问题，只是说如果 20 世纪 80 年代的趋势继续下去，我们现在已经处于平等地位了。

paragraphs.sourceText: It’s possible, however, that the journey towards wage parity would have stalled either way. If women’s gains in the 1980s were made through the erasure of things like bias, once those less uncontrollable problems had been addressed, there would still have been an issue with women — who are the ones to bear children and take care of them in the early weeks because of biological factors like the ability to breastfeed, forcing them to take breaks, whether or not those breaks were mandated.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，无论哪种方式，实现工资平等的进程都有可能陷入停滞。如果 20 世纪 80 年代女性的进步是通过消除偏见等问题取得的，那么一旦那些不那么无法控制的问题得到解决，女性仍然会面临一个问题——由于母乳喂养等生物学因素，她们是生孩子并在孩子出生后几周照顾孩子的人，这迫使她们休息，无论这些休息是否是强制性的。

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 关于 20 世纪 80 年代美国的性别工资差距，我们了解到什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. What prevents women from achieving parity with men in the final analysis?
paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 归根结底是什么阻碍了女性实现与男性的平等？
